newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tatarstan, Russia work on KamAZ debt.
newsitem.headline: Tatarstan, Russia work on KamAZ debt.

text.p: The governments of Russia and the Republic of Tatarstan, a semi-autonomous Russian region, are working on ways of paying off credits that Tatarstan heavy truck producer KamAZ has received from Moscow, Tatarstan's president said on Tuesday.
"The republic will act as a guarantor and the Economy Minister and the Finance Ministry are now working on the mechanism," Mintimer Shaimiyev told a news conference.
KamAZ received big government reconstruction loans after a fire brought its main engine production to a halt in 1993.
Shaimiyev said the unreconciled part of the credit amounted to 1.44 trillion roubles.
The federal government last year threatened KamAZ with bankruptcy due to 85 billion roubles in unpaid taxes.
The company managed to fend off the threat after the Tatarstan government agreed to pay KamAZ's debts.
The federal government owes Tatarstan 300 billion roubles, in outstanding budgetary payments.
"KamAZ is close to the times when its production will become competitive," Shaimiyev said. "No matter how hard it is we must support KamAZ and put it on its feet."
